headline: 41 accused in 2013 Shapla Square massacre: Sheikh Hasina and General Aziz among those named
summary: Prosecution has received the investigation report for the 2013 Motijheel killings, naming former PM and former Army Chief among 41 accused.
details: The prosecution has received the investigation report for the 2013 killings at Motijheel's Shapla Square. Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, former IGP Benzir Ahmed, and former Army Chief General Aziz are among the 41 people accused in the case.
caption:
41 people, including former PM Sheikh Hasina and former Army Chief General Aziz, are now accused in the 2013 Shapla Square massacre case.

The prosecution has received the investigation report for the 2013 killings at Motijheel's Shapla Square. Former Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, former IGP Benzir Ahmed, and former Army Chief General Aziz are among the 41 people accused in the case.

headline_marked: Netanyahu [[supports Argentina in World Cup final]]
headline: Netanyahu supports Argentina in World Cup final
summary: Israeli PM Benjamin Netanyahu backs Argentina against Spain, a move analysts say is driven by political alignment over the Palestine-Israel conflict.
details: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has publicly declared his support for Argentina in the World Cup final. The announcement came during a meeting with Rabbi Shimon Axel Wahnis, the Argentine ambassador to Israel.
During the meeting, the ambassador delivered an audio message from Argentine President Javier Milei, who described Netanyahu as a friend and thanked him for wishing Argentina victory.
Netanyahu responded by calling Milei a 'true friend' and a 'great friend,' stating that Israel stands by Argentina on many issues, including the upcoming final match.
Political analysts suggest the support is more about political diplomacy than sports. They point to the contrasting positions of Spain and Argentina regarding the Palestine-Israel conflict.

Spain has been vocal in its international opposition to Israeli aggression and has recognized Palestine as a state. In contrast, President Javier Milei has maintained a strong pro-Israel stance since taking office.
caption:
A World Cup final becomes a political stage. Why is Benjamin Netanyahu backing Argentina?

Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu has publicly declared his support for Argentina in the World Cup final. The announcement came during a meeting with Rabbi Shimon Axel Wahnis, the Argentine ambassador to Israel.

During the meeting, the ambassador delivered an audio message from Argentine President Javier Milei, who described Netanyahu as a friend and thanked him for wishing Argentina victory.

Netanyahu responded by calling Milei a 'true friend' and a 'great friend,' stating that Israel stands by Argentina on many issues, including the upcoming final match.

Political analysts suggest the support is more about political diplomacy than sports. They point to the contrasting positions of Spain and Argentina regarding the Palestine-Israel conflict.

Spain has been vocal in its international opposition to Israeli aggression and has recognized Palestine as a state. In contrast, President Javier Milei has maintained a strong pro-Israel stance since taking office.
